note: Public claims that AGI has already been achieved, and how each claim fares under the main definitions. Predictions of future AGI are excluded.

definitions.strict: This site's strict bar: at least 80% of remote professional tasks, including multi-week projects, done reliably.
definitions.levels: DeepMind's "Levels of AGI": general "Competent" (50th percentile of skilled adults) across most tasks.
definitions.charter: OpenAI charter: highly autonomous systems that outperform humans at most economically valuable work.
definitions.v2: Definitions v2.0 (agi.html): full human cognitive autonomy; all eight parts met at once; physical work out of scope.

claims.who: Eddy Keming Chen, Mikhail Belkin, Leon Bergen and David Danks
claims.role: UC San Diego faculty in philosophy, AI and data science, and linguistics
claims.quote: insofar as individual humans possess general intelligence, current LLMs do too
claims.venue: Nature Comment, "Does AI already have human-level intelligence? The evidence is clear" (quote: Chen, via UC San Diego Today)
claims.narrowDef: General intelligence judged by the standard we apply to individual humans; UC San Diego's summary: "by reasonable standards, current large language models (LLMs) already constitute AGI".
claims.interest: Academic authors; Bergen is also on the technical staff of Goodfire AI, an AI company (Nature's author note).

claims.narrowDef: Fridman's bar, which Huang accepted: an AI that could start, grow and run a tech company worth over $1B.
claims.interest: Sells the chips that AI is trained on.

claims.role: Physicist and arms-control analyst; says he coined the term "AGI"
claims.quote: I INVENTED THE TERM and I say we have achieved AGI
claims.venue: Post on X (reply to another user)
claims.narrowDef: Current models perform at "roughly high-human level in command of language and general knowledge" and work "thousands of times faster"; he adds that "some major deficiencies remain but they're falling fast".

claims.quote: AGI is here already. It's just not in a form that we appreciate
claims.venue: Interview with TechCrunch (published Apr 8), on winning the 2026 ACM Prize in Computing
claims.narrowDef: None stated; he added: "We should stop trying to apply human standards to these AI models."
claims.interest: Databricks sells a data and AI platform that companies use to build with these models.

claims.quote: We believe that AGI is already here
claims.venue: Keynote, Databricks Data + AI Summit, San Francisco (via SiliconANGLE)
claims.narrowDef: None stated in the reports we read; he added "AI does not have an intelligence problem right now. It's plenty smart."
claims.interest: Databricks sells a data and AI platform that companies use to build with these models.

claims.quote: for many tasks, we could say that we've already achieved AGI
claims.narrowDef: "In a lot of ways, and for many tasks"; in the same answer he called AGI milestones "kind of senseless at this point".
claims.interest: Sells the chips that AI is trained on.
